## Description:

UPC connect component seems to have upgraded and required a password authentication retrieve the connected devices. This was not necessary before the upgrade of the UPC connect box.

**Related issue (if applicable):** fixes #26490

**Pull request with documentation for [home-assistant.io](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io) (if applicable):** home-assistant/home-assistant.io#10317

## Example entry for `configuration.yaml` (if applicable):
```
device_tracker:
  - platform: upc_connect
    password: YOUR_ADMIN_PASSWORD
```

## Checklist:
  - [x] The code change is tested and works locally.
  - [x] Local tests pass with `tox`. **Your PR cannot be merged unless tests pass**
  - [x] There is no commented out code in this PR.
  - [x] I have followed the [development checklist][dev-checklist]

If user exposed functionality or configuration variables are added/changed:
  - [x] Documentation added/updated in [home-assistant.io](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io)

If the code communicates with devices, web services, or third-party tools:
  - [ ] [_The manifest file_][manifest-docs] has all fields filled out correctly. Update and include derived files by running `python3 -m script.hassfest`.
  - [ ] New or updated dependencies have been added to `requirements_all.txt` by running `python3 -m script.gen_requirements_all`.
  - [ ] Untested files have been added to `.coveragerc`.

If the code does not interact with devices:
  - [x] Tests have been added to verify that the new code works.

[dev-checklist]: https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/en/development_checklist.html
[manifest-docs]: https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/en/creating_integration_manifest.html

**Home Assistant release with the issue:**
<!--
- Frontend -> Developer tools -> Info
- Or use this command: hass --version
-->
0.99.0.dev0


**Last working Home Assistant release (if known):**


**Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):**
<!--
Please provide details about your environment.
-->
Tested on Windows/linux, virtualenv, python 3.7

**Component/platform:**
<!--
Please add the link to the documentation at https://www.home-assistant.io/components/ of the component/platform in question.
-->
upc_connect


**Description of problem:**



**Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml` entries and (fill out even if it seems unimportant):**
```yaml
device_tracker:
  - platform: upc_connect
    host: 192.168.1.1
```

**Traceback (if applicable):**
```
2019-09-07 09:41:52 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.upc_connect.device_tracker] Receive http code 302
2019-09-07 09:41:52 WARNING (MainThread) [homeassistant.components.upc_connect.device_tracker] Can't read device from 192.168.1.1
```

**Additional information:**
When trying to use upc_connect component, which was working fine about 2 weeks ago, no devices are marked as present and component gives the error above. I suspect that firmware upgrade of the router might have caused the issue, but I'm not 100% sure as UPC is not releasing too many info about upgrades and these are ussually silent. I have restarted both HA and router numerous times, upgraded HA twice etc. I have also tried another [python library](https://pypi.org/project/connect_box/) which communicates with this type of router without success. 
I can imagine that UPC updates the firmware because of the fact, that it's kind of a bug to be able to get DHCP table without any authentication to the router.
comments:
Thank you !
Just a quick mention - The UPC router allows only one connection at a time. By adding the password and having HA logged on the upc router, the router is not accessible anymore by the user.
If we want to make any change to the router we need to disable the upc_connect and restart HA and the router.

Would it be possible to add a "logout" function to this component? 
I presume that logging out after each query for devices, with a interval of 1 minute or so will alleviate this issue.

Thank you again!

I have just discovered the same issue as @Flopescu. The worst is that you HAVE to restart your router with HA already switched off if you want to make any changes otherwise you're unable to login. Logout option would be a really nice feature.

We need to be fair, after you setup is done, you don't need login many times to router.

That is an not supported API they we use for this. It is what it is.

@pvizeli, that is not quite true. There are many different situations when you want to access your router. Even if you access your router once a month. The fact that you have to stop HA is ok, but you need to reset the router and that is not convinient at all. The whole `upc_connect` plugin uses unsupported api for this router, so why not to act clean and use this api one more time to logout from router?
I checked the [this](https://github.com/fabaff/python-connect-box/blob/master/connect_box/__init__.py#L18) repo and there seems to be this functionality present already.
Fist, you will see, that I'm add that function. Second, we do what you said. The API is very unstable, so this function call work only in 50% of cases.

Thank you..let me know if I can help. One small example how important is to log out. I wanted to check unstability of the API with a little test (100 logins/logouts) but I simply cannot, because I'm unable to login to my router and I'm also unable to restart it because I have no physical access to it.
I hope UPC will read this and add an open API for his products. I know it's not nice now but I was not able to seen a better way with reverse engeenering.

I just wanted to bump pvizeli about logging out after each successfull login to the router, but I first went thru the code and discovered this:
``` python 
async def _shutdown(event):
        """Shutdown event."""
        await connect_box.async_close_session()
hass.bus.async_listen_once(EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_STOP, _shutdown)
```
which logouts from the router once you stop homeassistant. Good news is, that this works..there's no need to restart router to be able to log in.  Maybe this helps someone in the future.
